description: Measured and published performance of each boat's modern original, which go run ./tools/polar -check compares the physics with. Winds are in knots at each boat's height, in metres: a dinghy's at sail height, about 3 m, where wind measured from a dinghy is usually measured, the game's wind, 10 m up, scaled to it by the open sea's logarithmic profile; a rated keelboat's 10 m up, where a VPP rates it and the game's own height. Speeds are in knots. A point's tolerance is a fraction of its value; an 'atMost' point fails only when the boat is faster than tolerance allows above it.

notes: 7 October 2026, first calibration, in this order.

Sail (tools/polar -sail): maxLift 1.40 to 1.48, stallAngle 22 to 28, stallWidth 10 to 20, sailDrag 0.022 to 0.026, the normalForce table fitted, and twistEased (new) 20. ORC's mainsail gains drag fast as the boom eases (viscous drag 0.11 at 60°, 0.38 at 90°); on a Laser the mainsheet also holds the boom down, so easing it opens the leech. Drive is now within 4% of ORC's from 28° to 180°, side force within 4% at 28° and 60°. Beyond 60° an attached and a stalled trim give nearly the same drive, so the side force is not fitted there.
pressureAttached 0.30 to 0.33: ORC's centre of effort, 33% of the foot aft of the mast.

Weather helm: downwash (new) 0.5, the middle of the range for a rudder behind a keel or board; boardPosition 0.25 to 0.45. Weather helm is 0.1° at 9 knots, 0.7° at 12 and 1.7° at 15, growing with heel, but below the 2° to 4° of a real dinghy: further forward the board would no longer be where a Laser's is.

Accidental gybes: headBacked (new) 90 and headBackedWidth (new) 20. A sail as rigid strips, pressed on its sheet, never gybes before about 90° by the lee; a real one's backed head swings across and its leech drags the boom over. Accidental gybes now come 16° to 25° by the lee from 6 to 18 knots.

Flattening: from 6 to 11 m/s (was 12), down to 0.62 (was 0.65), against Day's upwind VMG at 12 knots: 3.71 knots against 3.73. The boat still heels 6° to 10° there, where Day's is held at 2° to 3°: the towed resistance is upright only.
The drag area above 9 knots is unchanged: the beam reaches are within 10% of Binns.

Sailor: rollRateGain 0.3 to 0.6, since at 0.3 the automatic sailor let the boat death-roll running in 22 knots. sailorDrag (new) 600, the sailor in the water holding on, and hiking while climbing back in: without them a righted boat rolled straight over the other way. swimTime 5 to 10 and climbTime 2 to 4: righting now takes about 15 s from falling in, within the 15 to 45 s of a real capsize.

notes: 7 November 2026, first calibration, in this order, from the first estimates.

Sails (tools/polar -sail). The main keeps the Jolly boat's fit to ORC's low-lift mainsail, its source too; twistEased 10 to 18, so that eased it gives ORC's drive: within 3.5% from 28° to 180°, side force within 3.5% at 28° and 60°. The headsails are fitted to ORC's low-lift jib (Table 5.4) from 27° to 100°: headsailMaxLift 1.5 to 2.1, headsailStallAngle 25 to 17, headsailStallWidth 20 to 19, headsailDrag 0.02 to 0.034, the normal-force table fitted, headsailTwist 6 to 8, headsailTwistEased 10 as it was; and headsailOut 60 to 20, the clew stopped at the rail, about 0.9 m out at the end of the 2.75 m foot. A jib's drag grows fast as it is eased (ORC's viscous drag 0.25 at 50°, 0.35 at 60°): only a clew stopped near the rail, its flow partly separated, gives it. Drive is within 3% of ORC's from 27° to 100°, side force within 4% at 27°, 50° and 60°. From 150° aft ORC's jib gives drive 0.82 to 0.90, as if poled out square to the wind; ours, sheeted to the rail behind the main, gives 0.3 to 0.5, and is not held there.

The righting lever: from a simple hull heeled in still water (sections from the plan at the sheer, the certificate's freeboards, a canoe body 0.30 m deep, the cuddy, the fin and its lead), its centre of gravity set for the certificate's 15.9 kg·m at 1° and its sections' fullness for its 105° limit of positive stability; then the sailor's 80 kg seated on the centreline, 0.93 m above the water. Its greatest lever is 0.41 m from 40° to 60°, where the cuddy's top meets the water; the limit falls to about 100° with the sailor. The first estimate (0.53 m at 50°) was stiffer than the certificate's limit allows.

Weather helm: boardPosition 0.10 to 0.9, the fin under the mast (1.14 m ahead of the centre of gravity) with its centre of pressure a quarter of its chord aft; downwash 0.5 to 0.8, a deep fin close ahead of the rudder. At 0.10 the boat carried 4° of lee helm upwind; now the helm is within a degree of neutral close-hauled and 1° to 4° of weather helm reaching in a breeze: light, as the Jolly boat's.
Accidental gybes: headBacked 90 and headBackedWidth 20, the Jolly boat's, already give 18° to 22° by the lee from 6 to 18 knots (tools/polar -manoeuvres).

The drag area, before the flattening since the reaches above 12 knots were over the rating: below 5 knots lowered by about 15% (0.033 at 3.5 knots), toward the canoe body's friction alone by ITTC 1957; from 5.5 knots steeper, 0.053 at 5.5, 0.068 at 6, 0.0965 at 7, 0.112 at 8 knots, the hump of a hull past its hull speed (a resistance of 3.6% of her weight at 6 knots and 7% at 7).

Flattening: flattenFrom 6 to 8, flattenTo 12 to 11, flattenMin 0.62 to 0.6 (ORC's floor), against the beat VMG: full power to 12 knots, where the rated crew still sits the boat up and one sailor nearly does, and flattened fully above, where one sailor carries less righting moment than the rated crew. The beat VMG is 4% to 8% under the rating from 6 to 12 knots, and under the rating above.

The autopilot (gain 2 to 3.5, damping 0.8 to 2): at the Jolly boat's values a stormy spell's gusts turned her up to 4.6° off a beam reach; now she holds within 1° rms and 3° at most, and tacks in 4.6 s keeping 66% of her speed.
The start sheet [[90, 0.5], [110, 0.6], [130, 0.7]] from tools/polar -start: each within 85% of the best sheet's speed 20 s from rest in 3, 5 and 8 knots.

Where she differs from the rating: from 90° aft the rating sets a spinnaker, which she has not: 3% to 26% slower there. Heel costs her hull nothing, as the Jolly boat's (the towed resistance is upright only), so in 20 knots her beat VMG, 4.13 knots, is near the rating's with the full crew; flattening alone holds it under.

notes: The mizzen boom: boomHeight 5.0 to 7.0, 2 m over the quarterdeck, so the boom and the foot of the gaff sail clear the helmsman at the wheel (her model's deck is set by her helmsman's place). Every reference still passes; at 7.4 the tack from 2.5 knots no longer stalled under the autopilot's rule but turned through, so it stays at 7.

8 November 2026, first calibration, in this order, from the first estimates. Her published values are kept: her length, beam, draught of 3.4 m, displacement of 550 t and her plain sail's area, about 910 m² in the game's groups.

The tool first. Its helmsman and times were a dinghy's: a ship slow to answer her helm and her sails (her hull's drag takes over a minute to change her speed) is steered meeting her turn as far ahead as her wheel takes, 9.6 s, with a standing helm it learns, begins each sail at 30% of the wind's speed and settles for as long as her hull takes to change her speed there, 2 to 8 minutes, and her braces are searched every fifth of their travel and then about the best. A point where her square sails are aback or lifting, where she is out of hand (her helm held past half its travel) or going more sideways than ahead, is not sailed, and her VMG is the one she makes good over the ground, her leeway in it. The Jolly boat's and the keelboat's polars, -check, -manoeuvres, -start and -sail are unchanged.

Square sails (tools/polar -sail): Tadano, Ohsugi, Amemiya and Yoshimura (1991), Figure 9, a foremast of six square sails, CLmax 1.01 at 30° (their text: 1.03), falling gently, its drag 0.88 square to the wind. The main's coefficients (a lift rising as a sine from nothing, a separated force across the sail) could not follow its straight rise from a lift of 0.08 along the yards to 0.97 at 25°, nor its force past the stall tilted some 10° toward lift off the sail's normal: the best fit missed by 7%. The square sails' lift and drag are now tables every 5° of attack from the figure's points (squareLift, squareDrag; the greatest lift, the stall angle and width and the drag removed), within 0.1% at every point; aback, the normal force the resultant of their drawing, 0.88 to 1.10. squarePressure 0.4 to 0.1: their centre of lateral force stays within a tenth of their width of the mast (Figure 9's l_p'). Lifting, for the crew, below the attack at which the lift is a quarter of its greatest, 4.8°; stalled past 1.75 times the attack of the greatest lift.

The mizzen and the headsails keep the main's and the jib's coefficients as the other boats fit them; trimmed in her rig, whose induced drag is three times a sloop's, they are shown against ORC's by -sail but not held. effectiveHeight 26 to 31 m, about the main truck's height, as the keelboat's is her masthead's.

The lateral plane. At first she spun round on every heading: her keel, 1.4 m under a 2.0 m body, gave a quarter of the side force a hull of her proportions gives (Clarke, Gedling and Hine 1983), while the Munk moment took its whole potential value, 370,000 kg. hullDraught 2.0 to 0.8 and boardSpan 1.4 to 2.6 m, the keel and deadwood the foil to her full draught; carryOver 1.0 to 3.9, the body above it carrying its lift; rudderSpan 2.4 to 2.6 m to the keel's depth and rudderChord 2.2 to 2.0 m. Her leeway close-hauled is now 8° to 10° in 10 to 20 knots.

A long hull's resistance to turning, yawDamping (new; 0 for the other boats, whose foils damp their turning): 86,000,000 N·m per (rad/s)², ½ρ C_D T L⁴/32 with C_D 2 on her 3.4 m draught and 29.8 m waterline. Without it a tack's turn carried her on round with no way to stop it.

Balance: boardPosition 2.0 to −1 m, munk 370,000 to 180,000 kg, headsailArea 160 to 120 m² (jib 40, fore topmast staysail 35, spritsail 45: two reefs still take the spritsail in at a share of 0.79), the 40 m² taken from them the staysails between the main and mizzen masts, counted with the after group (squareAfterArea 395 to 435 m², its centre squareAfterMast −0.34 to −0.71 m). With the lateral plane's centre forward, as a merchant hull's is (Clarke and others 1983), she rounded up into the wind whenever a tack or a wear left her slow and sliding sideways, and tacked back; with less Munk moment and her keel's lift a metre aft of her centre of gravity, she carries 4° of lee helm close-hauled and none reaching, and pays off after a tack. The settings that carried weather helm close-hauled failed a tack or a wear in 12 knots.

Pointing: braceSharp 30 to 42°. At 30 she pointed 55° to 60° off the wind; at 40 her best VMG was at 60° in 20 knots; at 42 it is 65° in 10, 15 and 20 knots (70° in 6), as the best ships sailed six points (Willis 2003).

The hull's drag, against the replica's passages: from 7.5 knots steeper, 3.5 m² at 8 knots to 11.5 at 12, the bow wave of a bluff collier's hull past a Froude number of 0.24: she makes 7.5 knots on the quarter in 15 knots and 8.0 in 18 (with the drag steepening only from 8 knots, 8.2 in 18), and 8.3 at most off the wind in 20.

The crew: braceTime 40 to 30 s, the wind helping the yards round; hauls 15° and letGo 25° (two points) kept. Her headsails' sheets are let fly in a tack until the fore yards come round, and the after yards are hauled to the new side as her head turns on past the wind, not only coming up to it.

The autopilot (tools/polar -manoeuvres and the behaviour tests): rudderInflow 0.8 to 1.0, her deep rudder meeting the water at her own speed: at 0.8 it could not hold her gathering way after a tack or a wear. steerage 0.5 to 1.5 m/s: from under 3 knots a tack stalls and she pays off on her old tack (from 2.5 knots in 12 knots of wind, after 20 s), with her full speed of 4.3 knots she comes round, within 5° of close-hauled on the new tack in 91 s. gybeHelm 0.6 to 1.0: her wear takes 109 m from where it began at the furthest, under four of her lengths (133 m; at 0.6, 131 m, too near them). gain 2 to 3 and damping 10 to 20: close-hauled in a stormy spell within 0.9° rms and 2.5° at most (at the first estimates 1.2° and 3.6°), and a wear from a broad reach keeping 80% of her speed. byTheLee 30 to 20°: her mizzen's boom gybes by itself 24° to 27° by the lee in 12 and 18 knots.

Stability, kept: a metacentric height of 1.2 m (her lever 0.21 m at 10°), the greatest lever 0.68 m at 50°, a range of 110°. A 40-knot gust braced up sharp lays her over to 27°; laid on her beam ends with her braces let go she is back under 30° in 2.8 s.

Reefing: she reefs from 27 knots, the wind in which close-hauled at full sail she heels past 10° (Beaufort's topgallants in at force 6, 22 to 27 knots); reefed she heels less (12.8°, 11.3° and 9.0° in 30 knots) and makes more to windward with two reefs (1.70 knots against 1.54).
The start braces [[90, 0.3], [110, 0.65], [130, 1]] from tools/polar -start, each within 95% of the best after 20 s from rest in 3, 5 and 8 knots.

Where she differs from her original: no stability booklet or polar of hers is published, so her references are her logged passages and the seamanship of square rig. Her speed falls steeply past 8 knots in flat water by her drag table, which holds her to her passages' speeds; in a sea she would surf, as she did at 13 knots in 2012. Her lateral plane is a foil and the Munk moment, tuned for her balance, not measured.
